items.stem:
These are the first four terms of a sequence.

7    11    15    19

parts.t: Write down the next two terms of the sequence.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.

sols: The terms go up by the same amount each time: 11 − 7 = 4, 15 − 11 = 4, 19 − 15 = 4.
19 + 4 = 23 and 23 + 4 = 27, so the next two terms are 23 and 27
The common difference is 4, so the rule starts with 4n.
the coefficient of n is the common difference
4n gives 4, 8, 12, 16 … and each term of the sequence is 3 more.

items.stem: The nth term of a sequence is 5n − 2.

parts.t: Write down the first three terms of the sequence.
Work out the 20th term.

One term of the sequence is 198.
Find the position of this term.

items.stem: Write down the next term of each of these sequences.

parts.t: 3   6   12   24   …
1   4   9   16   …
2   3   5   8   12   …

sols: Each term is double the one before: 6 ÷ 3 = 2, 12 ÷ 6 = 2, 24 ÷ 12 = 2.
a geometric sequence with common ratio 2
The differences are 1, 2, 3, 4, so they increase by 1 each time.
The next difference is 5, so the next term is 12 + 5 = 17

items.stem:
These are the first four terms of a sequence.

31    27    23    19

parts.t: Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.
Find the value of the first term of the sequence that is negative.

sols: the sequence goes down by 4 each time
So the rule is −4n + k for some number k.
n must be a whole number, so the first negative term is the 9th.
Check: the 8th term is 35 − 32 = 3, which is still positive ✓
ms:
M1 for −4n seen or common difference −4 stated
A1 oe

M1 for 35 − 4n < 0 or for n = 9 identified
A1 FT their linear nth term

items.stem:
These are the first five terms of a sequence.

3    8    15    24    35

parts.t: Write down the next term of the sequence.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.

sols: The first differences are 5, 7, 9, 11, so the next difference is 13.
constant second difference, so the sequence is quadratic
The n2 coefficient is 2 ÷ 2 = 1, so start with n2.
ms:
M1 for second difference 2 or n2 term identified
M1 for subtracting n2 to reach 2, 4, 6, 8, 10
A1 oe, e.g. n(n + 2)

items.stem:
These are the first four terms of a geometric sequence.

4    12    36    108

parts.t: Write down the common ratio.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.
Work out the 8th term of the sequence.

sols: Divide any term by the one before it: 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
A geometric sequence has nth term arn−1, where a is the first term.
ms:
M1 for arn−1 with a = 4 or r = 3
A1 oe, e.g. 4⁄3 × 3n

items.stem:
The diagram shows the first three patterns in a sequence made from sticks.
Pattern 1 uses 4 sticks, Pattern 2 uses 7 sticks and Pattern 3 uses 10 sticks.

parts.t: Work out the number of sticks in Pattern 4.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the number of sticks in Pattern n.

One pattern in this sequence uses 100 sticks.
Find the pattern number.

sols: Each new square adds 3 more sticks: 4, 7, 10, …
The numbers of sticks form a linear sequence with common difference 3.
So the rule is 3n + k; when n = 1, 3 + k = 4, so k = 1.

items.stem:
These are the first four terms of a sequence.

1⁄2    2⁄5    3⁄8    4⁄11

parts.t: Write down the next two terms of the sequence.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.

sols: The numerators are 1, 2, 3, 4, going up by 1.
The denominators are 2, 5, 8, 11, going up by 3.
The next two terms are 5⁄14 and 6⁄17
Denominators 2, 5, 8, 11 have common difference 3, so the nth denominator is 3n − 1.

items.stem:
These are the first five terms of a sequence.

5    12    23    38    57

parts.t: Write down the next term of the sequence.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.
Work out the 20th term of the sequence.

sols: First differences: 7, 11, 15, 19, which go up by 4 each time.
The next difference is 23, so the next term is 57 + 23 = 80
Second differences are all 4, so the sequence is quadratic.
ms:
M1 for second difference 4 leading to 2n2
M1 for 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or n + 2 seen
A1 oe

items.stem:
These are the first five terms of sequence A.

8    14    22    32    44

The nth term of sequence B is 5 × 3n−1.

parts.t: Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of sequence A.
Show that 158 is a term of sequence A and write down its position in the sequence.
Find the first term of sequence B that is greater than 10 000.

sols: constant second difference, so sequence A is quadratic
That is linear with common difference 3 and nth term 3n + 4.
n = 11 or n = −14; a position must be a positive integer.
The 7th term is 5 × 3<sup>6</sup> = 3645, which is too small.
ms:
M1 for second difference 2 leading to n2
M1 for 7, 10, 13, 16, 19 or 3n + 4 seen
A1 oe

M1 for n2 + 3n − 154 = 0 oe or for correct trial reaching 158
A1 nfww

items.stem:
The first term of a sequence is 3.
The term-to-term rule is ‘multiply by 2 and then subtract 1’.

parts.t: Write down the next three terms of the sequence.
Explain why 100 cannot be a term of this sequence.

sols: apply the rule to each new term
Every term is 2 × (something) − 1, which is always odd.
an even number minus 1 is odd
100 is even, and every term of the sequence is odd, so 100 cannot be a term.
the terms are 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, 65, 129, … and 100 is skipped over
ms:
B1
e.g. all terms are odd; or 65 then 129 jumps past 100

items.stem: The nth term of a sequence is 6n − 1.

parts.t: Show that 89 is a term of the sequence and write down its position.
Explain why 100 is not a term of the sequence.

sols: n is not a whole number, so 100 is not a term.
the 16th term is 95 and the 17th is 101, so 100 is missed
ms:
M1 for 6n = 101 or n = 16.8… oe, or for 95 and 101 seen
A1 for stating n is not an integer, oe

items.stem:
These are the first four terms of a sequence.

1⁄2    1⁄4    1⁄8    1⁄16

parts.t: Write down the next term of the sequence.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.

sols: Each term is half the term before.

parts.t: Write down the next term of the sequence of cube numbers 1,  8,  27,  64,  …

These are the first four terms of another sequence.
2    9    28    65
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.

sols: Compare with the cube numbers 1, 8, 27, 64: each term is 1 more.
ms:
M1 for n3 seen or for comparing with 1, 8, 27, 64
A1 oe

items.stem: In each of these sequences, each term after the second is the sum of the two terms before it.

parts.t: Write down the next two terms of the sequence 2,  5,  7,  12,  19,  …
Find the value of x in the sequence 4,  x,  11,  18,  …

sols: add the two previous terms each time
The third term is the sum of the first two: 4 + x = 11

items.stem:
The triangular numbers are

1    3    6    10    15    …

parts.t: Write down the next triangular number.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth triangular number.
Work out the 30th triangular number.

sols: The differences are 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next difference is 6.
Second differences are 1, 1, 1, so the sequence is quadratic with n2 coefficient ½.
½n2 gives ½, 2, 4½, 8, 12½; subtracting from the sequence leaves ½, 1, 1½, 2, 2½ = ½n.
ms:
M1 for ½n2 seen or second difference 1 used
A1 oe, e.g. (n2 + n)⁄2

items.stem: In a linear sequence, the 3rd term is 14 and the 7th term is 30.

parts.t: Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of the sequence.
Work out the 50th term.

sols: From the 3rd term to the 7th term is 4 steps, and the terms rise by 30 − 14 = 16.
a linear sequence rises by the same amount each step
So the nth term is 4n + c. When n = 3: 12 + c = 14, so c = 2.
ms:
M1 for (30 − 14) ÷ 4 or common difference 4
M1 for 4n + c with 3rd term used
A1 oe

items.stem:
A ball is dropped and each bounce reaches half the height of the previous bounce.
The heights of the first four bounces, in centimetres, are

320    160    80    40

parts.t: Find an expression, in terms of n, for the height of the nth bounce.
Find the first bounce whose height is less than 1 cm, and state its height.

sols: This is a geometric sequence with first term 320 and common ratio ½.
each height is half the one before
The 9th bounce is 1.25 cm, still more than 1 cm.
The 10th bounce is the first below 1 cm, with height 0.625 cm
ms:
M1 for r = ½ identified or 320 × (½)k with any k in terms of n
A1 oe, e.g. 640 ÷ 2n

M1 for 1.25 or 0.625 seen, or 320 ÷ 2n−1 < 1
A1 both correct

items.stem:
These are the first five terms of a sequence.

3    5    9    17    33

parts.t: Write down the next term of the sequence.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.
Work out the 12th term.

sols: The differences are 2, 4, 8, 16, which double each time.
not linear or quadratic: the differences are powers of 2
Next difference is 32, so the next term is 33 + 32 = 65
Each term is one more than the matching power of 2.
ms:
M1 for 2n seen or powers of 2 compared
A1 oe

The diagram shows the first three patterns in a sequence made from dots.
Pattern n has n rows of dots.
Pattern 1 has 2 dots, Pattern 2 has 6 dots and Pattern 3 has 12 dots.

parts.t: Work out the number of dots in Pattern 4.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the number of dots in Pattern n.

One pattern has 132 dots.
Find the pattern number.

sols: Pattern 4 has 4 rows with 5 dots in each row.
each row has one more dot than the pattern number
Pattern n is a rectangle of n rows and (n + 1) columns.
Check: 2, 6, 12, 20 have differences 4, 6, 8 and second difference 2, matching n2 ✓
Solve n(n + 1) = 132: two consecutive integers with product 132.
ms:
M1 for n × (n + 1) or second difference 2 used
A1 oe, e.g. n2 + n

items.stem:
The nth term of a sequence is n2 + an + b, where a and b are integers.
The 2nd term is 11 and the 4th term is 29.

parts.t: Find the value of a and the value of b.
Work out the 10th term.

ms:
M1 for 4 + 2a + b = 11 oe
M1 for 16 + 4a + b = 29 oe and a valid elimination
A1 both correct

items.stem:
Sequence A has nth term 4n + 1.
Sequence B has nth term 6n − 3.

parts.t: Write down the first four terms of sequence B.
Find the first two numbers that are in both sequence A and sequence B.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth number that is in both sequences.

sols: The first two numbers in both lists are 9 and 21
The common numbers 9, 21, 33, … go up by 12 each time.
12 is the lowest common multiple of the two differences 4 and 6
ms:
M1 for at least five correct terms of A or 9 identified
A1 both correct

items.stem: A sequence is defined by u1 = 5 and un+1 = 2un − 3.

parts.t: Write down the values of u2 and u3.
Work out u5.
Show that un = 2n + 3 gives the same terms.
Find the value of n for which un = 1027.

sols: the formula matches all five terms found so far
which is the formula with n + 1 in place of n
so the rule always produces the next value of 2n + 3 and the two definitions agree.
ms:
M1 for at least three terms checked or 2(2n + 3) − 3 formed
A1 for reaching 2n+1 + 3 or all five terms verified

The first three terms are 3, 17 and 55.

parts.t: Find the value of a and the value of b.

1025 is a term of the sequence.
Find its position in the sequence.

ms:
M1 for a + b = 3 and 8a + b = 17 oe
M1 for eliminating one unknown
A1 both correct

items.stem:
A path is paved with grey and white square tiles. The diagram shows the first three patterns.
Pattern n has a square block of grey tiles surrounded by a border of white tiles.

Pattern1234
Grey tiles149
White tiles81216

parts.t: Complete the table for Pattern 4.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the number of white tiles in Pattern n.
Show that the total number of tiles in Pattern n is (n + 2)2.

One pattern uses 400 tiles in total.
Work out how many of these tiles are grey.

sols: Grey tiles are square numbers, so Pattern 4 has 4<sup>2</sup> = 16 grey tiles.
White tiles go up by 4 each time, so Pattern 4 has 16 + 4 = 20 white tiles.
8, 12, 16 is linear with common difference 4, so the rule is 4n + c; 4 + c = 8 gives c = 4.
the border has 4 sides of n tiles plus 4 corners
Grey tiles = n2 and white tiles = 4n + 4, so total = n2 + 4n + 4
Check: Pattern 3 is a 5 × 5 square of tiles = 25 = 9 + 16 ✓
the whole pattern is a square of side n + 2
ms:
M1 for n2 + 4n + 4 oe
A1 for correct factorising, or for identifying the (n + 2) by (n + 2) square, nfww
